p: The site itself is part of the story. Hendon was home to some of the earliest days of British aviation, and among the buildings you'll find the Grahame-White Factory and Watch Office, historic structures linked to the pioneering years of the airfield. It's worth a look even if you're mainly there for the aircraft.

How long should you allow? With several hangars to explore, most visitors find a good few hours flies by. Aviation fans could easily spend the whole day, so don't plan anything too tight afterwards. Comfortable shoes are a good idea, because there's a fair bit of walking between the different buildings.

For families, pace the visit with breaks. Mix the big halls full of aircraft with time in the play area, and let kids pick out a favourite plane to look out for. It's a great way to keep younger ones engaged in what can be a big museum.
If your family catches the aviation bug, the RAF Museum has a second site at Cosford in Shropshire, which makes for a great follow-up trip if you're ever in the Midlands.

Getting here is simple. Colindale Tube station on the Northern line is a short walk away, and if you're driving, the museum is close to the M1 and the A41. Being in north London, it's away from the busiest tourist crowds, so it can feel much more relaxed than museums in the centre.
Nearby, Brent Cross is handy for shopping and food, and the wider Hendon area has parks and green spaces if you fancy a breather in the fresh air afterwards.
